subject: Clarify: training exclusion + retention/playbook details

Subject: Quick Q: do you train on customer content? + retention details

Hi Maya,

We're working through a sensitivity review ahead of an integration pilot. Two quick asks we need to clarify before legal signs off:

1) Does Redwood ever use our customer-provided content to train models or update base model weights?
2) What are the retention timelines for request/response logs, debug snapshots, and backups?

We may have PHI in certain prompts during the pilot; BrightHealth requires clear commitments and a deletion/playbook for any retained artifacts. If you have a short summary and any supporting artifacts (SOC2 note, deletion playbook), can you share?

Thanks,
Ellie

Subject: Re: Quick Q: do you train on customer content? + retention details

Hi Ellie — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then detail below.

Topline: Redwood does not train public model weights on customer content by default. For the modes you mentioned:
- Hosted API: Customer content is not used to update model weights or training corpora unless a customer explicitly opts into a model-improvement program (we do not enable this on pilot customers by default).
- Dedicated: Tenant data is isolated to your pool and not used for model training.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Customer controls data and no data leaves the environment for model training.

Retention summary (default configs):
- Request/response logs: 30 days (configurable per contract for Dedicated/Private).
- Streaming tokens / KV cache: ephemeral within the inference runtime (seconds-minutes), not persisted as training artifacts.
- Debug snapshots & traces: retained for up to 7 days by default and marked for deletion after investigation; can be reduced to 0 days on request.
- Backups / snapshots (storage-level): periodic backups retained for 30 days; long-term archival only with customer consent.

I've attached a SOC2 overview and our deletion playbook stub for review.

Attachments: [attachment: SOC2-overview.pdf (pdf)], [attachment: deletion-playbook-2028-11.pdf (pdf)]

If you want, I can pull Dev (our compliance engineer) and Grace (security) into a short call to walk through evidence and contract language.

Best,
Maya Srinivasan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick Q: do you train on customer content? + retention details

Hi Ellie — jumping in with technical detail for legal:

1) Training on customer content: We have two distinct flows. Operational telemetry and aggregated, de-identified signals (latency, error rates, token counts) are used internally for system performance tuning and are not fed into model training corpora. Any use of customer content for model improvement requires an explicit opt-in workflow with contractual scope, dataset controls, and an opt-in flag at the account level. That opt-in is audited and reversible.

2) Deletion and audit trail: Our deletion workflow:
- Tombstone: Data is marked as deleted in the primary store immediately at request. This operation is recorded in an immutable audit log entry (requestor id, timestamp, object ids).
- Purge: Primary storage objects are scheduled for physical purge within 48–72 hours (configurable in enterprise agreements).
- Backups: Snapshot backups are rotated; worst-case retention window is the next backup rotation (default 30 days). We can offer a contractual shorter backup retention for Dedicated and Private deployments (e.g., 7-day backup window).
- Evidence: For Dedicated/Private we can provide deletion confirmation artifacts and an audit log extract. For Hosted we provide an attestation and log extracts on request (subject to support process and verification).

3) Debug snapshots / traces: Debug snapshots used for reproducing an incident are isolated, access-controlled, and scrubbed for PII where possible. By default retained 7 days; can be configured down to immediate deletion after use.

4) Edge caches and KV stores: Per-request caches are in-memory and evicted; we do not persist them to any training store.

If you need contract-ready wording, we can propose a short clause and have Legal iterate.

- Dev (Compliance Engineer)
